notes: Offer document for EFT's 50% tender at 99% of NAV. Two events: (1) the tender itself; (2) the three 'Subsequent Conditional Tender Offers' the Board authorized under the same Saba agreement, which the filing describes with their terms but says the Offer to Purchase does not relate to. Conditional programme: one tender in Q4 of each of 2022, 2023 and 2024, triggered if the average discount from January to August of that year exceeds 10%. The window is stated only in months ('from January to August of that year'; the Exhibit (d)(i) agreement says e.g. 'from January 2022 through August 2022'), so window_start/window_end are null. Commencement date comes from the June 29, 2021 press release (Exhibit (a)(5)(i)), which says the funds 'announced today the commencement'. The same release's boilerplate also says 'The Funds have not commenced the Tender Offers described in this release', which contradicts it. The withdrawal-rights text (August 25, 2021 = 40 business days from commencement) agrees with June 29. The Board's approval was conditioned on certification of shareholder approval of the new advisory agreement; the filing says that condition was met (certified May 12, 2021), so shareholder_approval is not listed among the open conditions. The condition that new federal or state limits on bank credit, and a banking moratorium, would stop the offer was folded into market_disruption. 'other' = the asset-coverage condition on senior securities. The Offer is not conditioned on any minimum number of Shares tendered. The press release names other Eaton Vance funds (EVG, EFR, EVF); only EFT's offer is extracted. 39,863,690 Shares were outstanding as of June 23, 2021.
